content.jointProblem: Can uncertainty-aware matching of farm policies to radar-derived hail footprints improve exposure estimates and identify potentially underpriced portfolio segments compared with municipality-level rating? The first experiment would test location recovery and hail-intensity proxies on held-out storms and claim years, separately for crops and buildings, before considering automated pricing integration.

rationale.text: The researcher has directly relevant experience developing parcel-scale hail hazard maps and evaluating them against agricultural insurance losses in Vojvodina.

sources.quote: This study develops probabilistic hail hazard maps at 1 km resolution
The maps were validated against parcel-level crop loss reports provided by the insurance cooperative Vojvodina Agro-Protect covering 14,000 parcels over 2015–2019.

rationale.text: He has prior insurance-industry experience using radar products for cadastral-parcel hail premium zoning.

sources.quote: сарађивао је са осигуравајућом кућом Агропрот д.о.о. из Новог Сада на пројекту зонирања премија за градобитно осигурање усева
коришћени радарски производи за процену учесталости и интензитета туче на нивоу катастарских парцела.

rationale.text: His published work supports testing radar–satellite fusion and storm tracking for the company's narrow, moving hail footprints.

sources.quote: This study presents a cell-tracking algorithm that fuses dual-polarisation C-band radar parameters with Meteosat Second Generation SEVIRI brightness temperatures
Detected cells were tracked using a modified TITAN algorithm over a 400 × 400 km domain.

rationale.text: His project portfolio includes documented Python processing and spatial-data delivery, providing a relevant starting point for an automated workflow rather than manual GIS overlays.

sources.quote: Core deliverables included the benchmark dataset of 18 agroclimatic indices (2001–2020), a Web Map Service interface, and a documented open-source Python processing chain.

constraints.text: Policy-to-field matching must resolve settlement-only addresses where possible and preserve location uncertainty where it cannot; settlement centroids cannot be treated as verified insured-field coordinates.

sources.quote: a large share of our farm addresses are stored only at the settlement level, not as coordinates.

constraints.text: Field-scale hail estimation requires a weather-data feasibility gate: assess the existing daily 5 km product and secure suitable historical radar inputs before adopting the researcher's radar-based approach.

sources.quote: We do receive daily gridded weather data from MeteoVoj d.o.o. at a five-kilometre resolution
using a 15-year (2005–2019) archive of dual-polarisation radar data

constraints.text: Initial validation must work within three claim years and approximately 1,200 farm policies; this limits independent storm/year holdouts and the strength of conclusions about underpricing.

sources.quote: We have three full claim years with geo-tagged loss data for about 1,200 farm policies to work with.

constraints.text: The deliverable must support automated pricing input through the existing Python batch workflow, not stop at a GIS map.

sources.quote: turning that into something that feeds the pricing model automatically is beyond what our team can do alone.
Python-based batch scoring pipeline for quarterly rating factor refresh

constraints.text: Implementation and maintenance must fit the company's shared operational staffing; a named pricing owner and IT owner are needed for the pilot.

sources.quote: a four-person pricing team and a six-person IT team who split their time between operational support and new product build.

constraints.text: Scheduling must respect the researcher's stated earliest start of September 2025 and competing field-campaign leadership; his current availability still needs confirmation.

risks: The validated hail maps concern crop losses, not farm-building damage, and 1 km hazard surfaces do not establish individual-field accuracy. The first experiment must test transfer separately by insured asset type and location quality.

Detecting hail-bearing cells and using MESH-derived proxies do not establish ground-level damaging hail intensity at each insured location. Initial validation needs independent hail observations where available, not claims alone.
Daily 5 km weather fields may not resolve narrow hail tracks; access, licensing, cost and historical coverage of suitable radar data are unknown.
Settlement-only policy addresses may remain unresolvable even when claims are geo-tagged, creating biased exposure assignments or excluding less well-documented policies.

Three claim years may contain too few independent damaging storms for stable pricing conclusions. Hazard alone cannot explain the reported 18% excess without accounting for insured values, coverage, vulnerability and claim-cost changes.

Current researcher capacity, project budget, delivery deadline and company data-sharing permissions are unknown. Limited company implementation capacity and the earlier unintegrated flood prototype create a risk of another standalone mapping output.
questions: Can policies be linked to cadastral parcels, insured-building coordinates or field polygons, and what exactly do the existing claim geotags locate?
What variables, timestamps and hail-specific information does MeteoVoj supply, and can historical radar or MESH products be licensed for all three claim years and operational reuse?
Are full exposure records available, including non-claiming policies, premiums, sums insured, deductibles, asset types, coverage periods and event dates?
What independent hail observations are available, and can the first pilot use storm/year holdouts, location-quality strata and separate crop/building assessments against the municipality baseline?
What uncertainty reporting, actuarial review, data-protection controls and approval process are required before any new factor affects pricing?
Who will own the Python integration and maintenance, and what budget, computing resources, delivery timeline and acceptance criteria can the company commit?
What is the researcher's current availability and team capacity for a joint project, given the field-campaign responsibilities recorded in his notes?
